biur-halacha/3:_: There is none nowadays forbidden — see Mishna Berurah: since not expert treat as full chametz; Ritzh Giat laws R' Sherira: even though sages said chalut etc. boiling water strongly rolled — we do not rely to act unknown how guard from chimutz; perhaps cools from corner and causes chimutz — not heard in two yeshivot who permitted except sick and animal per experts saying cure; if not — danger; or if matzah would endanger — only chalut in boiling feed immediately, eat immediately, leave nothing; Rav Hai Gaon there: chalita in boiling surely matzah; but all early rabbis generations: this chalita we do not know how it is — never permitted chalut in dough; much effort permit barley boiling for sick — Geonim did not permit permitted chalita. For sick, early Geonim ruled when ill cannot taste anything Pesach and endangered — permitted per doctors "in all one is healed except idolatry"; Maharam Chalavah; after Rav Hai, Rav Alfasi explained more — forbidden all like other prohibitions standing in judgment; sick with danger permitted, not otherwise. These prove forbid chalita even b'dieved, benefit; since like other prohibitions; explicit: sick without danger we do not lighten — expanded to refute Magen Avraham's uncertainty perhaps only l'chatchila; had he seen predecessors would not doubt; proof from liver — Avot Rabbi Natan rejected. Wonder at Radbaz Chayei Adam 141 asked permit sick drink barley water — perhaps Geonim stringency only dough that hurries chametz before water boils; hard barley they did not decree chalita; even if decreed, sick etc. rely on our expertise barley dry strong — even sick without danger I would permit; Geonim explicit also barley remedy; explicit sick without danger not permitted; Machatzit HaShekel: without danger; his words wondrous; responsum sides leniency place boiled barley even without danger — supported Chayei Adam; appears thought Chayei Adam permits keep after Pesach even in kind — not so — only mixture something as Mishna Berurah; Gra same; chalut in kind certainly forbidden keep — R' Sherira: leave nothing; therefore do not lighten against Geonim; do not give sick barley water unless endangered; chalut barley on stomach as Mishna Berurah — Geonim themselves stringent only drinking lest karet taste; placing on stomach only concern "lest be seen" — perhaps not stringent; all sick they permitted; what difference lav and karet prohibition — uncertain:
chok-yaakov/1:א: In bread of sovin not bread of mursan. Sovin and mursan are same — sovin is thick hull of grain, mursan thin; Rashi Shabbat ch. 7 and Ra'avad ch. 2 Challah; Peirushim on Terumot opposite; Magen Avraham: somewhat proves causes chimutz since fulfill per Rif; possible since species that causes chimutz — fulfills obligation; saw mursan called shafiryar does not chametz — but hard hull; wheat hull itself perhaps causes chimutz; impossible no wheat substance adheres — end Magen Avraham (see Peirushim Terumot mishnah 5: new wheat sovin much flour mixed, not old — Ra'avad). I wonder at his uncertainty — why doubt? Complete mishnah: do not soak mursan for chickens — causes chimutz siman 465; how hidden from him? If oat spike found in dissolved food without grain — perhaps wheat fell in — see Torat HaShelamim; all fell at harvest time we do not establish prohibition; rabbinic something — Machatzit HaShekel s.k. 5; if three spikes need examination:
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [1] Sovin etc. Magen Avraham: saw mursan called shafiryar does not chametz — but hard hull; wheat hull itself perhaps causes chimutz; impossible no wheat substance adheres. Chok Yaakov wondered his uncertainty — mishnah: do not soak mursan for chickens — causes chimutz siman 465. In my humble opinion Magen Avraham uncertain only wheat hull (sovin), as he wrote Rashi: sovin wheat hull at threshing, mursan remains in sieve; Rambam opposite per Ramban Shabbat ch. 7 — nevertheless no difficulty for Magen Avraham who wrote per Rashi only. Apparently difficult on Rashi Terumot ch. 11: mursan permitted, new sovin forbidden — if Rashi why mursan permitted and sovin forbidden if sovin inferior? Also difficult Rambam — if mursan inferior, mishnah Shabbat ch. 7 mursan and sovin do not join — Tosafot Pesachim 39 clear not taught so; can resolve first on Rashi: sometimes call sovin what is mursan and vice versa from above difficulty. Resolves Ramban Terumot did not bring Rashi, stam like Rambam; Shabbat like Rashi; stam ch. 2 Challah like Rambam because there sovin and mursan join — difficult per Rashi "this and need not say this"; Tosafot Yom Tov did not address. Practically: hard hull certainly causes chimutz; thick hull all new within thirty days causes chimutz; after thirty days no flour mixed per Ramban Terumot ch. 11; however Shibolei Leket 62 Rashi: also sovin causes chimutz. Chok Yaakov: oat spike in dissolved food without grain — all fell harvest, do not establish prohibition — see Magen Avraham end 465; if three spikes in remainder need examination:
eshel-avraham/1:_: Mursan. Per Rif one fulfills — therefore some proof it causes chimutz — Magen Avraham; also wheat hulls chametz; impossible no substance adheres — see Terumot ch. 11 mishnah 5:
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) Magen Avraham wrote: saw mursan shafiryar does not chametz — hard hull; wheat hull perhaps causes chimutz; impossible no substance — Chok Yosef sign 1; Chayyim sign 1 wondered at Magen Avraham — complete mishnah do not soak mursan for chickens, woman not speak mursan — certainly causes chimutz siman 465 — see there. Avot Rabbi Natan sign 1: Magen Avraham uncertain only wheat hull (sovin) as opening Rashi; Yad Efraim hagahot: Magen Avraham only sovin, mursan certainly causes chimutz — see there. Chayei Adam klal 122 sign 2; explained further 465 — see there:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: And it is possible etc. Kaf HaChayyim wrote: I wonder on this — did we not learn a complete mishnah: one may not soak mursan for chickens, nor may a woman speak meat with mursan, and it certainly causes chimutz as below siman 465 — end quote in brief. In Avot of Rabbi Natan it says Magen Avraham was uncertain regarding sovin that are inferior to mursan per Rashi's explanation; and although Rambam explains opposite to Rashi that mursan is thick and sovin thin — nevertheless Magen Avraham wrote his words per the explanation he brought — see there. In my humble opinion Magen Avraham certainly agrees sovin and mursan chametz, for it is impossible a little flour not adhere to them, as he concludes this s.k. Therefore one does not soak for chickens nor does a woman speak with them; rather he was uncertain whether mursan and sovin themselves chametz, therefore Maharil inferred Rif holds one fulfills with bread of sovin — so sovin themselves chametz. Nafka mina: if sovin or mursan fell into a dish after noon until night, then it is batel as written above siman 447. Against a little flour adhering to them — some say if sovin themselves do not chametz, the dish is permitted. What he concludes "and also impossible not adhere" — his intent: one must distinguish between shafiryar and wheat hull itself; those who permitted shafiryar would not permit wheat hull itself, for Magen Avraham knows those mursan they permitted even on Pesach forbid in any amount, or on erev Pesach and there is no view; if so with wheat hull itself — even though it does not chametz by itself, nevertheless forbid because of adhering flour, as proven from "one does not soak mursan":
machatzit-hashekel/4:ב: And removed immediately permitted the water — ChM: what difference if removed immediately or after time, for if we rely on chalita even if it stayed long time there is nothing, for it will not chametz again; in my humble opinion he wrote immediately to include Rabbi Akiva YD siman 73 that the reason we are not expert is perhaps they will not boil well; Bach there added we are not expert in measure of water whether little or much; Bach further added we are not expert how long it stays in boiling water; further added — if so for our latter uncertainty how long it stays — implies even if expert in water measure and also expert in boiling measure that is proper — nevertheless concerned perhaps must leave it inside longer than they placed; if so all the time the dough is in boiling — for us too no concern perhaps partition; but afterward when removing dough from boiling — concerned perhaps needed leave in boiling more and dough still not chalut and still can chametz. Nevertheless if dough stayed in boiling long time — forbid the boiling water perhaps dough still not chalut and it is all the time water boils — why concern it will chametz? Nevertheless perhaps water cooled somewhat from boiling and still was not chalut — if so at that time water cooled perhaps it became chametz; therefore Magen Avraham wrote even if removed immediately and they know at that short time it did not cool from boiling — if so should permit also for us even though not expert how long stays in boiling; nevertheless from other uncertainties Rabbi Akiva and Bach wrote — forbid:
magen-avraham/3:_: To perform chalita — they would chalut the dough in boiling water and thereby it does not chametz; nowadays we are not expert in chalita — so too YD siman 73 regarding liver; and apparently just as he ruled there b'dieved permitted, so too if a piece of dough fell into boiling water at time of boiling and removed immediately — b'dieved permitted; and so implies somewhat Tur siman 461 and 467 that grain was in water before boiling and became chametz — implies somewhat at time of boiling it does not chametz; nevertheless do not lighten since not found explicit in poskim:
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (13) Forbidden — in eating and benefit; likewise forbidden to keep it, for since we are not expert we are concerned it is full chametz; if mixed in a dish it forbids in any amount; nevertheless Acharonim wrote regarding chalita one does not forbid the dish in any amount except eating, not benefit; likewise keeping permitted in such case. Acharonim further wrote: one with stomach illness whose cure is chaluting barley or oats and placing on stomach — if this illness occurred on Pesach with danger, Israel may do via chalita — boil water well then put grains in — even with danger, wherever possible on lenient side do so; if no danger — forbidden even via chalita, for since not expert when chaluting there is concern it will be seen became chametz; if a non-Jew does from his own or Israel transfers barley before chalita — permitted even without danger; if possible chalut in fruit juice — permitted even by Israel without danger, for in fruit juice it does not chametz — see Biur Halacha. Chayei Adam wrote: when soldiers pass on Pesach and force Israel to cook groats for them — if can appease to cook buckwheat — good; at minimum sift grain kernels in them; if cannot appease and they give barley groats — if can save himself with money, obligated per ability; if not — Israel should be careful at least to do chalita: cook water beforehand until much boiled, then put groats little by little so water not cool; good also with buckwheat; but oat groats are full chametz as known — end quote:
mishnah-berurah/4:ה: (18) And regarding blessing see etc. — meaning there explained for blessing in all cases one does not bless even where acquired — it is "one who cuts blesses, reviles the Name"; no difference between blessing of eating matzah and hamotzi itself; regarding birkat hamazon see above siman 196 seif 1 in Mishna Berurah:
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Magen Avraham s.k. 1) Somewhat proves it reaches chimutz. NB: difficult — did we not learn a complete mishnah daf 59: one does not soak mursan because they chametz?
shaarei-teshuvah/4:_: Stolen. Ba'er Hetev; see responsum Bach Chadashim and Kaf Alef — good to say gift formula; Sha'agat Aryeh 92–93 expanded: even who holds no bereirah helps; no concern "stole and owners not despaired" — since not in his reshus after mistaken exchange; also there helps forgive and give gift to robber himself — see 94: his view maror stolen fulfills since maror now rabbinic — not concern cooking; Rama 649 stringent; nevertheless stolen matzah does not work second Yom Tov night though rabbinic — see there. Shulchan Aruch seif 1 do not knead etc. even matzah not mitzvah — concern chimutz Rashbatz essay chametz and responsa 82:7; money filled pool at night do not knead — brought in R' Yonah:
turei-zahav/4:_: In stolen matzah. In Ashkenazi he derives ch. 20 from that which they say regarding ma'aseh sheni one does not fulfill — R' Meir plainly; but regarding etrog not so plain, for one can say "for you" excludes borrowed and stolen; but ma'aser sheni not excluded — not so matzah where written twice "your doughs" — excludes also ma'aser sheni; if so all the more borrowed and stolen. Therefore we should say: just as stolen matzah invalid, so borrowed matzah — for regarding etrog they are compared; except truth is not so — etrog is different, for it returns in kind; even so in his hand not called his — general borrowing in his hand; but one who borrows matzah from friend intended to eat it and payment he owes is in place of it or another matzah — this is now truly his, only debt in hand to pay — like one who borrowed money from friend for expenditure and betrothed with it — surely betrothed, since money does not return in kind and he has money in hand; so in my humble opinion one fulfills with borrowed matzah; I do not know for etrog here; and it is a fortiori from stealing flour with guilt in hand:
